description: Queries events with SQL across every ticker or a screen's matches: earnings, dividends, splits, filings, insider trades and analyst actions, plus opt-in estimate revisions, news and signal firings. Requires at least one bound: a ticker scope (ticker/universe) or a time window (from/to); `q` alone is not a bound. With one `kind`, its payload fields are bare names in `q`/`select`/`group_by` (`q: firm ILIKE 'Morgan Stanley'`, `q: relevance >= 0.8` on news); tickerbot_list_event_kinds lists them. `join: state` adds the ticker's signals as of each event. Every result has a stable `id`: use it to drop duplicates. `kind: signal` takes custom signals too.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor from the previous response. It carries the filters, `dir` and `select`, so pass it alone. A `q`, `ticker` list or `select` too long to ride in it is kept as a fingerprint instead: send that param again with `cursor`, the same as on the first page (`q_truncated` flags `q`). A missing or different value is a 400 naming the param. Not valid with `group_by`.

dir.description: A list: `desc` (default) is newest first, `asc` oldest first, paging forward. With `group_by`: the rollup's sort direction.

from.description: Events at or after this instant, in strict ISO: `YYYY-MM-DD` or `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM[:SS]Z`. A bare `YYYY-MM-DD` means from the start of that day. For news, analyst ratings and estimate revisions the day is the ET calendar day (a story at 21:00 ET on Nov 2 is Nov 2); dated kinds use their own dates. For `signal`, the ticker's home-market day: ET for stocks and ETFs, UTC for crypto, FX and rates.

grain.description: Only with `kind=signal` or `join=state`. With `kind=signal`, the grain the flips are read at: `1m`, `1h` or `1d`, or `auto` (the default), the coarsest grain the signal is stored at. With `join=state`, the grain the ticker's signals are read at: `auto` (default) blends hourly and the last closed daily session per event; see as of a past date.

group_by.description: Comma list of rollup keys; it switches the response to rollups. Columns (`kind`, `ticker`), payload fields (`firm`, or the explicit `payload->>'firm'`) and expressions over them all roll up. Name a key with `AS` to choose its JSON key: `payload->>'firm' AS firm`. Un-named keys are named for you: a payload read takes its key (`payload->>'firm'` → `firm`), a function keeps the function's name (`lower(ticker)` → `lower`), and anything else falls back to `group_1`, `group_2`.

join.description: Set to `state` to use the ticker's signals in `q`, `select`, `group_by` and `having`, read as of each event's timestamp at the grain `grain` picks. On the daily grain an event on day D reads D-1's row, never D's close. A signal and a payload field with the same name (`price` on insider and signal events, `cik` on filing) resolve to the signal; spell the field `payload->>'price'`. Needs `q`, `group_by` or a ticker signal in `select`.

kind.description: Comma list of kinds. Leave it out for earnings, dividend, split, filing, insider and analyst. News, signal and estimate_revision come back only when named. List event kinds lists each kind, its fields and its filters. Values: dividend, split, insider, analyst, earnings, filing, signal, news, estimate_revision.

limit.description: Page size for a list (default 50): up to 1000 until 2027-01-12, then 100, and the rest pages with `next_cursor`. A `group_by` rollup returns every group up to `limit` (default and max 1000) and sets `truncated: true` when there are more. A larger value is clamped to the max, not an error; see Deprecations.

merge_gap_seconds.description: Only with `kind=signal`. Merges an exit and re-entry closer than N seconds into one span. Needs one `signal` and a `ticker` list, and does not combine with `q`, `group_by` or `join=state`.

order.description: With `group_by`: the rollup sort, a bare column or output name (put expressions in `select` and sort by their alias); a group key's name works too: `group_by=payload->>'firm' AS firm&order=firm`. Default: `events`, or with your own `select`, its last column's alias. A list is sorted by `ts`: `order=ts` is accepted there and changes nothing.

q.description: SQL WHERE over `id`, `ticker`, `ts`, `kind` and `payload` (plus the ticker's signals with `join=state`). With one `kind`, its payload fields are typed columns by bare name: `amount > 1`, `firm ILIKE 'Morgan Stanley'`, `relevance >= 0.8` on news (List event kinds lists them); with several kinds, use `payload->>'…'`. Max 4000 chars. ANDs with the other filters.

select.description: Without `group_by`: what each result carries. `id`, `ticker`, `ts` and `kind` always, then the names you list, each at the top level of the result: `payload`, a payload field of the one kind named (`firm`, or `payload->>'firm'`) and with `join=state` a ticker signal. `*` is every field: the whole `payload`, and with `join=state` every signal the read's grain stores. With `group_by`: the rollup's output columns (default: the group keys + `COUNT(*) AS events`), named with `AS` or for you as on `group_by`.

signal.description: Only with `kind=signal`. One signal or a comma list of up to 5: built-in yes/no signals or your custom signals. Required with `q` or `join=state`. An unknown name filters nothing in and is listed in `not_found` (every name unknown: no signal events). See Signal firings.

ticker.description: One ticker or a comma list (up to 50). Not combinable with `universe`. A crypto, FX or rate symbol (`X:BTCUSD`) takes `kind=signal`; every other kind is equities-only and returns `400` naming the symbol's asset class.

to.description: Window end, in the same strict ISO subset. A bare `YYYY-MM-DD` means through the end of that day; a timestamp is exclusive (events strictly before it). For news, analyst ratings and estimate revisions the day is the ET calendar day; dated kinds use their own dates. For `signal`, the ticker's home-market day: ET for stocks and ETFs, UTC for crypto, FX and rates.

universe.description: Scope to a built-in universe (`top_10`, `top_100`) or one of your own, by id. An unknown one answers 200 with no results and its id in `not_found`. Not combinable with `ticker`.

name: tickerbot_query_events
